transcript.text: Samsung RS67A8810S9 fridge freezer display says OF OF and everything is getting warm. Fan's quiet. Has it broken?

Probably not broken. On Samsung fridge freezers, "OF OF" isn't a fault code. It means the cooling has been switched off: it's the demo or shop mode used in showrooms. That fits exactly with everything warming up and the fan being quiet. It usually gets turned on by accident, often by holding a couple of buttons together while cleaning the panel or changing a setting. 1. On most Samsung models you exit by pressing and holding two of the temperature buttons together for about 3 to 5 seconds. It's usually the Fridge and Freezer buttons, though on some panels it's a different pair. Hold them until you hear a beep and the display goes back to showing temperatures. Your user manual, or Samsung's online manual for your model, will confirm which pair it uses.
2. If that doesn't clear it, switch it off at the wall for about 5 minutes. Then turn it back on and try the button hold again.
3. Once it's back to normal, check the settings are right: fridge around 3 to 5°C and freezer -18°C. Then keep the doors shut so it can recover. It will take several hours to get properly cold, and up to a day for the freezer. A word on the food. If the fridge has been above about 8°C for more than a few hours, throw out high-risk items like meat, fish, dairy and leftovers. Freezer food that has fully thawed shouldn't be refrozen. If it still has ice crystals and still feels freezer-cold, it's usually fine to refreeze. If "OF OF" clears but it still isn't getting cold after a day, that's a different problem. Then we'd look at whether the fan runs and whether ice has built up at the back of the freezer. If the code won't clear at all, the control board may be the issue, and that's a job for Samsung or an engineer. Let me know how you get on with the buttons.

I tried the button combination from the manual and it chimed and the display shows temperatures again. The fridge thermometer said 9C though, and I'm worried about the milk and chicken. Should I throw them out?

Good news: the chime and the temperatures coming back mean it's out of demo mode and cooling again. Nothing was broken. On the milk and chicken, it depends on how long they've been warm. 9°C is just over the 8°C limit for chilled food. 1. Raw chicken: if it has been above 8°C for more than about 4 hours, or you don't know how long, throw it out. Chicken is the highest-risk item, and the bacteria that matter (salmonella, campylobacter) don't change how it looks or smells. If you're certain it has only been warm for a short time, it's fine to cook it thoroughly today. If there's any doubt, bin it.
2. Milk: it's lower risk than chicken. If it's unopened and only went warm recently, it's usually fine. If it's opened, or has been warm for many hours or overnight, I'd replace it. A sniff test catches souring, but it isn't a reliable safety check.
3. Other high-risk items such as cooked leftovers, cooked meats, soft cheese and ready meals: use the same 4-hour rule as the chicken.
4. Freezer: anything that has fully thawed shouldn't be refrozen. Cook it today or throw it out. Food that still has ice crystals is fine to leave in. While it recovers, keep the doors shut as much as you can. It can take several hours for the fridge to drop back to 3 to 5°C and up to a day for the freezer. It's worth checking your thermometer again later today. If the fridge still isn't below 5°C after about 24 hours, let me know and we'll look at the cooling. To stop it happening again, wipe the display with the panel locked if your model has a child or control lock. Otherwise use a damp cloth with light strokes rather than pressing, because holding two buttons together is what usually triggers demo mode. Is there anything else I can help with?

claimsRejected.claim: In this mode the lights and display work, but the compressor and fans don't run.

candidates: Cooling-off (demo/shop) mode switched on, so the compressor and fans aren't running (high)
A genuine cooling fault (fan, defrost or sealed system), only if it still won't cool once the mode is off (low)
plan: They asked: "Has it broken?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Samsung; model RS67A8810S9; code OF OF.
The fault they reported is: "everything getting warm". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.

candidates: Demo / cooling-off mode accidentally switched on (now cleared) (high)

The customer says it is fixed: say so warmly, give one short tip to stop it happening again, and ask if there is anything else.
